text:
To: Event Committee
From: Valentina Cruz, Conference Organizer
Subject: Keynote speaker withdrawal

I regret to inform you that Professor Linde has withdrawn from the conference on account of a family emergency. [1] I have already contacted two alternative speakers, both of whom have extensive experience of the subject, and I expect to have confirmation by Friday.

In view of the short notice, we shall not be able to [2] the printed program, which went to press yesterday. Instead, a notice will be inserted in each delegate's pack. [3] the replacement has not been confirmed by the end of next week, I propose that we reorganize the opening session as a panel discussion, [4] the technical requirements are considerably simpler.

choices: The loss is unfortunate, but it is not an insurmountable problem, as the program has some flexibility in its opening session.
The loss is fortunate, but it is an insurmountable problem, as the program has no flexibility in its opening session.
The loss was unfortunate, but it was not an insurmountable problem, as the program had some flexibility in its closing session.
The loss of the program is unfortunate, but it is not a problem, as the speaker has some flexibility in his opening session.
questions.explanation: The next sentence reports that two alternative speakers have been contacted, so the previous one should present the withdrawal as manageable; only the first does coherently.
The organizer cannot 'amend' (change) the printed program; 'amass' means accumulate, 'amuse' means entertain, and 'ameliorate' means improve.
'In the event that the replacement has not been confirmed' introduces a possible situation; 'whereas', 'albeit' and 'inasmuch as' do not.
'Since the technical requirements are considerably simpler' gives the reason for the proposal; 'unless' and 'whereas' do not.
